subject: Next steps after demo — buyer, security checklist, procurement runbook
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@medsys.io>, Procurement <procurement@medsys.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2024 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's demo (latency/cost/security)

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned.

What we showed
- Live demo of Redwood inference with 95th-pctl latency under 200ms on the demo workload
- Cost/throughput tradeoffs across quantized vs FP configs
- Private deployment option (VPC) + per-route RBAC and audit logs

Key decision criteria you mentioned
- Economic buyer must be comfortable with predictable committed costs and burst behavior
- Security needs: SOC 2 evidence + data residency restrictions for PHI flows
- Contracting: MSA + SOW template review by procurement/legal

Asks / proposed owners
1) Sophie — can you confirm the economic buyer (name/title) and who will own the procurement/contracting lane?
2) Procurement — can you share your standard timeline and required artifacts for an initial commercial review?
3) Neha (cc) — please prepare a short performance profile (p95/p50/cost per 1k tokens) tuned for MedSys sample data; target by EOD Thu.
4) Lauren (cc) — I'll hand contracting to you once we have buyer & timeline.

Attachments: Redwood_Eval_SLA.pdf (summary SLA + performance guarantees)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-med-sys-eval (demo logs + sample config)

Proposed next meeting: 30-min procurement + security sync next week to align on docs and acceptance criteria.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_Eval_SLA.pdf (PDF, 246 KB)]
From: Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@medsys.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsys.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's demo (latency/cost/security)

Alex — great demo, appreciate the clarity. Short answers inline and next steps: 

Economic buyer / stakeholders
- Economic buyer: Daniel Ruiz, VP Product (daniel.ruiz@medsys.io) — he'll make the final purchasing decision.
- Security/Compliance reviewer: Monica Levine (monica.levine@medsys.io) — she'll run the SOC2/data residency checklist.

Procurement timeline / asks
- Procurement typically takes 3–4 weeks for an initial purchase (vendor review + legal redlines).
- We require: SOC2 Type II, data processing addendum, and a draft MSA/SOW for our legal team.
- Can you provide a redline-friendly MSA and a sample SOW? Also include an outline of support SLAs (response/priority).

Next steps
- I'll loop Daniel and Monica into the thread after I confirm times.
- Procurement (cc) — please confirm if there are any additional artifacts needed beyond the above.

Thanks,
Sophie Chan
Director, Platform Integrations | MedSys
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@medsys.io>, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@medsys.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@medsys.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's demo (latency/cost/security)

Thanks Sophie — welcome Daniel (copied). Quick replies and action items below.

Attachments included
- draft_MSA_annotated.docx (highlights on data residency & audit rights)
- Redwood_Eval_SLA.pdf (already attached; summary doc)

Security & compliance
- SOC 2 Type II report: we can provide our most recent attestation under NDA. Neha, can you confirm the expected timeline to share the report with MedSys?
- Data residency: for PHI we recommend Private deployment (VPC) in us-west region; Neha will outline what artifacts & controls we can present to Monica.

Commercial / contracting
- Lauren will be the lead on the contracting lane and will coordinate on redlines. Lauren — suggested path: initial MSA redline + a short SOW that defines POC acceptance criteria (3–4 measurable checks).

Operational / acceptance criteria (proposal)
- P95 latency < 250ms for the 2K token sample set (as run in demo)
- Throughput: sustained 20 rps at 99% of the time during business hours
- Accuracy/regression: pass the provided evaluation prompt set with >=95% pass rate on business-critical intents

Proposed meeting: Thu 2024-04-11 10:00 AM PT — 30 minutes (procurement + security + Alex/Neha/Lauren). If that works for Daniel/Monica/Procurement, we'll send a calendar invite.

Drive link with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-med-sys-eval
Attachments: draft_MSA_annotated.docx

Alex
[attachment: draft_MSA_annotated.docx (DOCX, 128 KB)]
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@medsys.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@medsys.io>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsys.io>, Monica Levine <monica.levine@medsys.io>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's demo (latency/cost/security)

Alex / Sophie — thanks, this is helpful. A few quick items from the buyer side to keep the procurement clock moving: 

1) Please upload a clean MSA (no annotations) and a SOW template to the Drive folder so our legal team can start an initial pass.
2) We need an operational runbook / handoff doc that covers: onboarding steps, roles & responsibilities, escalation contacts, and rollback criteria for the POC.
3) For the POC acceptance criteria, add an item for model behavior/sign-off from Product (we will provide a SME).

If you can get those artifacts into the Drive before EOD Fri (2024-04-12), procurement will begin internal intake next week and we can aim to complete contracting in ~3 weeks. Also confirm whether you support SOC2 under NDA or if you can post the report to a secure portal.

I'll tentatively accept the Thu 10:00 PT slot — Sophie, can you confirm?

Thanks — Daniel
VP Product | MedSys
